 Georgia social media influencer ‘Shawty Dred’ stole $4M in benefits with 350 fake SNAP accounts: Feds
 Atlanta-based Mercedes Reshard New facing federal fraud charges
 Francine Frazier , Senior Digital Producer
 Published:  October 26, 2026 at 11:13 AM Tags:  Atlanta , Georgia , Fraud , Money Social media personality Mercedes Reshard New, a/k/a “Shawty Dred,” was arrested on federal charges for fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. (Mug shot) ATLANTA – Atlanta social media personality “Shawty Dred,” real name Mercedes Reshard New, was arrested on federal charges accusing him of fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in food assistance benefits, prosecutors said.
 New, 39, was indicted Oct. 7 on 46 counts of mail fraud, 15 counts of aggravated identity theft and one count each of SNAP fraud and illegal transactions with access devices. 
 Recommended Videos
 New was arrested Oct. 13 and is being held by the U.S. Marshals Service pending further court proceedings.
 According to the indictment, New controlled more than 350 fraudulent Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program accounts between January 2020 and July 2026. 
 Prosecutors allege the accounts were opened using stolen identities, and that New arranged for electronic benefit transfer cards to be sent to addresses around metro Atlanta.
 New also allegedly sought and obtained authorization for the company Shawty Dred LLC to operate as a SNAP retailer. 
 From April 2024 to November 2025, prosecutors say, New used fraudulently obtained EBT cards and a point-of-sale device associated with the company to take more than $660,000 in benefits.
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture revoked the company’s retailer authorization in November 2025, according to prosecutors. About two weeks later, local police arrested New on allegations of selling SNAP benefits at a metro Atlanta store and seized 14 EBT cards issued to other people. 
 Prosecutors allege New later arranged for replacement cards to be sent to the store and other Atlanta-area addresses.
 Over the course of the alleged scheme, New caused Georgia’s Division of Family and Children Services to transfer about $4.6 million in benefits to the accounts, and EBT cards were used to take about $4 million from them, prosecutors said.
 Prosecutors also allege New displayed an extravagant lifestyle on social media, including posts showing private jets, Rolls-Royce and Maybach vehicles, and stacks of cash. 
 The Instagram account “richlifeshawtydred” has more than 2 million followers, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.
 “New allegedly stole over $4 million meant for poor families who need help putting food on the table,” U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said.
 SNAP provides monthly food benefits to eligible low-income households. Beneficiaries are prohibited from selling or trading those benefits.
 The charges are allegations. New is presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
